title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing p.2). Let E* be a ring with a Z-grading. Let π_i (i in Z, almost all zero) be elements of E. Formulas (1.2) define E^(ν) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} E π_i and pr_ν(u) = Σ_i π_{i+ν} u π_i.

Question. When do these formulas define on E a structure of graded ring?

Answer given. It suffices that the π_i form a complete finite family of orthogonal idempotents: π_i^2 = π_i, π_iπ_j = π_jπ_i = 0 for i≠j, and Σπ_i = 1.

Why it works. Then E has the two-sided Peirce decomposition E = ⊕_{i,j} π_j E π_i, with projections pr_{i,j}(u) = π_j u π_i, and u = Σ_{α,β} π_β u π_α. It follows that:
- the pr_ν are orthogonal projectors on E with sum 1, so E = ⊕_ν E^(ν) as groups;
- E^(ν)E^(ν') ⊂ E^(ν+ν'), because π_{j+ν'} ... π_i with mismatched middle indices vanish.

Criterion (1.4) also holds: u ∈ E^(ν) iff uπ_i = π_{i+ν}u for all i. Indeed uπ_i = Σ_β π_β u π_i and π_{i+ν}u = Σ_α π_{i+ν} u π_α. Comparing Peirce components gives π_β u π_i = 0 for β ≠ i+ν.

Side remarks.
- Margin (brown ink): Z may be replaced by an arbitrary group.
- Bracketed note: one should look at modules over E equipped with such π_i. Implicitly, these are graded modules M = ⊕ π_i M, so the situation of §1 (E ⊂ End of a graded module) is recovered.

§3 (new problem). Start from a graded ring E* and ask whether there exists a family (π_i) satisfying the idempotent relations that induces the given grading via (1.2)/(1.4), and whether it is unique.
- The next page adds the normalization π_i = 0 outside [0,2n]. This kills the trivial shift ambiguity π_i → π_{i+c}.
- It then proves uniqueness inductively from the extremes. It uses that E^0 is the commutant of the π_i, so the π_i are central in E^0, and that the corner π_{2n-i} E π_i is recoverable from the already-known π_α.

Purpose. Abstract the algebra of cohomological correspondences of a smooth projective n-dimensional variety. Its grading is by degree shift, and the π_i are the Künneth projectors (components of the diagonal). The aim is to know when the Künneth components are intrinsically determined by the graded correspondence algebra. This is the formal side of standard conjecture C, within the 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' formalism of this dossier.
errors: Equation labels are inconsistent with p.2. The idempotent relations are labelled (1.3) on p.2 but cited as (1.1) here, where (1.1) originally meant π_i ∈ E. In §3 the reference 'définissant la graduation par (1.3)' should be (1.2). These are cosmetic.

The stated condition is sufficient, as Grothendieck says ('il suffit'). It is not claimed necessary, and it is not, e.g. trivially when E has a different grading compatible otherwise. No mathematical error.

In §3 uniqueness cannot hold in general without further hypotheses. If E is block diagonal (M = M1 ⊕ M2 with no maps between them), the blocks can be shifted independently within the allowed interval. The next page's argument relies on knowledge of the corners π_{2n-i} E π_i, hence implicitly on a Lefschetz/duality-type nondegeneracy. That hypothesis is not yet stated on this page.

ideas.what: A complete finite family of orthogonal idempotents in a ring induces a group grading E^(ν) = Σ π_{i+ν} E π_i, with u ∈ E^(ν) iff uπ_i = π_{i+ν}u.
ideas.modern_name: Peirce decomposition / inner (idempotent-induced) grading; grading of a matrix-type ring End(⊕M^i)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Peirce (decomposition); standard in graded ring theory (e.g. Năstăsescu–Van Oystaeyen)

ideas.what: Replace Z by an arbitrary group in the grading.
Existence and uniqueness of idempotents (Künneth-type projectors supported in [0,2n]) inducing a given grading of a graded ring of correspondences.
ideas.modern_name: intrinsic characterization / uniqueness of Künneth projectors; standard conjecture C in an abstract algebra-of-correspondences setting
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures appear in Grothendieck 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) and Kleiman's exposés; this abstract uniqueness formalism itself unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins an abstract treatment of when a graded ring (modelling correspondences) admits a unique family of 'Künneth' idempotents supported in [0,2n] inducing its grading. The aim is a purely algebraic route to standard conjecture C. This page only sets up the problem; the hypotheses needed for uniqueness are not formulated here.
missed.quote: Partons enfin d'un anneau gradué E*, et posons nous la question de l'existence et l'unicité d'une famille (π_i) ... définissant la graduation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Questions of uniqueness and intrinsic determination of Künneth/Chow–Künneth decompositions remain live in motive theory (Murre, Kimura, André). An abstract graded-ring criterion is of minor historical interest, but the page content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine Peirce-decomposition argument setting up the grading-by-idempotents formalism. The only noteworthy aspect is its role as groundwork for an unpublished abstract approach to Künneth projectors, which is developed on later pages.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed 'Σ' throughout is Grothendieck's calligraphic E (the ring \mathcal{E}), not Σ. 'Sur Σ^(ν)' at the top should read 'sur \mathcal{E}^*'.
Line 1 continues the question from p.2: '...définissent-elles sur E* une structure d'[struck word] graduée ?' The struck word is probably 'algèbre', replaced by 'anneau'.
'donc que les E^(ν) définissent bien une graduation (de modules) sur E*' — the target is E*, not E^(ν).
'Notons aussi que (1.4.) que (1.4) soit valable' should read 'Notons aussi que (1.4) reste valable, car...'.
The margin note is in brown ink, a later addition: 'on peut remplacer Z par un groupe quelconque' (the last word is plausibly 'quelconque').
In §3 the inserted phrase reads 'satisfaisant (1.1.)' and 'définissant la graduation par (1.3.)', which is inconsistent with the earlier numbering.
